description: Main set with every // comment line removed. Used to measure how much comments describing the bug helped the LLM.

samples.name: SQL injection via string concatenation
samples.note: Clean source->sink taint flow. Static tools handle this well; the LLM mainly adds explanation.

samples.name: OS command injection via shell_exec
samples.note: The fix (escapeshellarg) still concatenates, so naive concat-based detectors false-positive on the fixed version. Recognizing the sanitizer requires understanding, not just a pattern.

samples.name: Path traversal via unvalidated filename
samples.note: Detecting the vuln is pattern-ish; confirming that basename() plus the is_file() check actually neutralizes it is reasoning.

samples.name: Mass assignment via request->all()
samples.note: Whether this is exploitable depends on the model's $fillable/$guarded config, which lives in another file. True confirmation needs cross-file context an LLM agent can gather but a single-file regex cannot.

samples.name: IDOR / broken object-level authorization
samples.note: There is no dangerous function call here at all. The bug is the ABSENCE of an ownership check. Pattern-matchers cannot see a missing thing; this needs reasoning about intent. Authorization CWEs (639/863/862/285) are all acceptable labels for it.
